scenes.title: 1978 CUNY Library Copy Alcove: 5 Pages ('Because I Have to Make Copies' = 93%!) vs 20 Pages (Crashes to 24%!)
scenes.era: 1978, CUNY Graduate Center Library, Manhattan, New York

layout.description: Sunlit high-key 1978 university library copy alcove featuring a classic beige freestanding **1970s Xerox console photocopier** with its warm green document glass lid raised, stacks of white bond paper, and a crisp two-column **Langer 1978 Copy-Line Scoreboard** comparing **5 Pages (No Reason 60% | Real 'Rush' 94% | Empty 'Because Make Copies' 93%!)** against **20 Pages (No Reason 24% | Empty 'Because' 24% | Real 'Rush' 42%)**.

positions.who: Langer Confederate mannequin (in 1978 corduroy blazer holding a thin **5-page packet**)
positions.where: stepping politely up beside the Xerox photocopier speaking the famous tautology ('...because I have to make copies?')

positions.who: Waiting Doctoral Student mannequin (in 1978 turtleneck sweater and glasses holding an open library volume)
positions.where: smiling automatically and gesturing 'Go right ahead!' at **93%** for 5 pages — while a second student beside the **thick 20-page stack** shakes their head 'Wait your turn!' (**24%**)

props.name: 1978 freestanding beige library Xerox photocopier + thin 5-page vs thick 20-page paper stacks
props.period_detail: makes the effort-cost switch visually unmistakable
props.physical_behavior: the exact Manhattan library setting of Langer, Blank & Chanowitz 1978

props.name: Langer 1978 2×3 Compliance Matrix Board ('5 Pages: 60% / 94% / 93% vs 20 Pages: 24% / 42% / 24%')
props.period_detail: shows BOTH the famous 93% 'because' shock AND the overlooked 20-page awakening

actions.verb_sequence: holds up 5 pages and says 'because I have to make copies' -> Library user steps warmly aside (93%!) -> Confederate returns holding a thick 20-page stack with the same empty 'because' -> Library user pauses, hears the hollow excuse, and shakes head NO (24%)!

reactions.who: Ellen Langer mannequin (observing discretely behind library bookshelves with a notepad)
reactions.reaction: smiles as the 5-page vs 20-page fork maps the exact boundary of human autopilot
blinks realizing they just let someone cut for 'having to make copies' at a copy machine

scenes.wardrobe: 1978 New York academic attire: tan corduroy jacket over collared shirt; ribbed knit turtleneck, wool slacks, and wire-rim spectacles.
scenes.lighting: Clean high-key Manhattan library tall-window daylight.
scenes.recognition_hook: Ask to cut in line at a library Xerox machine with five pages 'because I have to make copies,' and 93% of graduate scholars step aside — try that exact empty line with twenty pages and 76% shut you down cold!

key_visual.description: a sunlit 1978 university library copy alcove where a student holding 5 pages asks to cut at a beige Xerox photocopier beside a 93%-vs-24% compliance scoreboard

scenes.title: Studies 1 & 2: Why Routine Office Memos Run on Autopilot

layout.description: Bright 1978 university office desk with standard interoffice memo slips versus unfamiliar phrasing.

positions.where: comparing routine-format memos (90% automatic compliance) against novel-format memos that wake up critical reading

props.name: Familiar Script Memo vs Novel Format Memo
props.period_detail: shows scripts trigger via structural familiarity

actions.verb_sequence: stamps familiar-syntax memo automatically -> pauses thoughtfully on novel-syntax memo

scenes.recognition_hook: Before Langer ever walked up to the Xerox machine, two office-memo experiments proved familiar formatting puts smart adults on polite autopilot!

scenes.title: The 20-Page Wake-Up Call: Stake Size Flips Mindfulness ON

layout.description: Clean split desk contrasting Low Cost (20-second wait -> Autopilot 'Click-Whirr') vs High Cost (5-minute wait -> Active Scrutiny of Reasons).

positions.where: auditing whether the requester's reason is genuine and uncontrollable ('printer jammed before exam') versus lazy

props.name: Cost-Threshold Switch Card ('Low Stakes = Script | High Stakes = Logic')

actions.verb_sequence: weighs thick 20-page stack -> accepts genuine rush (42%), rejects hollow tautology (24%)

reactions.reaction: confirm human autopilot has a built-in price alarm

scenes.recognition_hook: Your brain isn't broken — it only runs the 'Because' shortcut on 20-second favors and wakes the lawyer up when someone brings 20 pages!

scenes.title: Everyday Upgrade: Give Honest 'Becauses' & Audit Hollow Ones

layout.description: Bright modern desk where a laptop message swaps 'Need this by 3 PM' for 'Could we wrap this by 3 PM **because** client review starts at 3:30?'

positions.where: exchanging a clear, genuine 'because' message that unlocks fast goodwill cooperation

actions.verb_sequence: adds one honest 'because' clause -> Teammate nods immediately and prioritizes it

scenes.recognition_hook: Never bark a bare deadline when one honest 'because' clause nearly doubles how gladly people help you!
